author: Angelica Cheyenne
title: Food Network packs line-up with holiday content after axing beloved Halloween programs - NewsBreak
text:
By Angelica Cheyenne ,
25 minutes ago Food Network has more than 50 hours of holiday content on deck in preparation for the upcoming holiday season following the death of network star Anne Burrell this summer.
The television station is lining up more holiday content after getting rid of three popular Halloween-themed cooking shows in September. Food Network recently unveiled its schedule up until Christmas, which will include a Guy Fieri special, and the return of the Holiday Baking Championship, and Bobby Flay: Holiday Throwdown. Guy will be hosting spinoff series, Tournament of Champions: All-Star Christmas.
Food Network is seeing many changes, like when the network's beloved star Rachael Ray had fans grieving the "end of an era" after she made her exit .

Food Network is also premiering a new show called Sweet Empire this holiday season. The series will have 14 chefs design edible artwork with their teams for the show's judges Jacques Torres and Yolanda Gampp.
While the network is bringing on new shows, its also going to be bringing back many beloved fan-favorites such as Harry Potter: Wizards of Baking, a show hosted by James and Oliver Phelps.
However, this go round, bakers will be back in the kitchen with former Harry Potter cast members such as Warwick Davis (Professor Flitwick), Afshan Azad (Padma Patil) and Devon Murray (Seamus Finnigan). The show is scheduled to return November 2.
Meanwhile, the Holiday Baking Championship is coming back on November 3, and is going to be hosted by Jesse Palmer with Duff Goldman, Nancy Fuller, and Kardea Brown serving as judges.
Food Network's Christmas line-up follows popular Halloween programs such as Outrageous Pumpkins, Last Bite Hotel, and Halloween Cookie Challenge being cut in September.
Halloween Cookie Challenge, which was hosted by Rosanna Pansino and Duff Goldman, debuted in 2022 and had two seasons.
The Damaris Phillips-hosted Outrageous Pumpkins ran for five seasons, and involved expert pumpkin carvers compete for the title Outrageous Pumpkins Champion and a prize of $50,000.
Tituss Burgess was the host of the Last Bite Hotel, which debuted last September. For that show, eight chefs were instructed to cook in a spooky hotel with the only 13 ingredients given. They had to work with those ingredients for the entire duration of their stay.
